attack.reasoning: The updates describe an internal service degradation and remediation, but they do not establish what caused it or say whether hostile activity was involved. The evidence therefore does not support classifying this as either an attack or not an attack.

findings.claim: Cloudflare initially characterized the event as an internal service degradation with intermittent impact to some services.
During remediation, Cloudflare disabled WARP access in London; London users trying to use WARP could not connect.
Cloudflare reported that changes allowed Access and WARP to recover, and that it re-enabled WARP access in London.
After Access and WARP recovered, Cloudflare was still working to restore application services; it later reported restoring dashboard services while broad application-services impact remained.
Cloudflare reported intermittent bot-score impact during global recovery and continuing errors and latency before later reporting improvement.
The published updates do not establish the underlying technical cause of the incident; they describe the degradation and recovery actions without identifying the initiating fault.

timeline.event: Cloudflare reported an internal service degradation and said it was working to restore service.
Cloudflare reported services recovering, while warning that error rates could remain elevated during remediation.
Cloudflare said it had disabled WARP access in London during remediation.
Cloudflare said it had identified the issue and was implementing a fix.
Cloudflare reported Access and WARP recovery and re-enabled WARP access in London, while continuing to work on other services.
Cloudflare reported that a change restored dashboard services, though broad application-services impact remained.
Cloudflare said a fix had been implemented and it believed the incident was resolved, while it continued monitoring.
Cloudflare reported intermittent impact to bot scores during global recovery.
Cloudflare said services were operating normally and elevated network errors and latency were no longer being observed.
The status incident was marked resolved; the resolved update's text is not provided.

root_cause.claim: The technical root cause cannot be determined from the published updates provided: they report an internal degradation, a fix, and recovery, but do not identify the initiating fault.

contributing_factors.claim: A documented remediation measure itself temporarily prevented London users from connecting to the Internet via WARP; Cloudflare later re-enabled access.

Recovery was staggered across services: Access and WARP recovered before application services and the dashboard were fully restored, and additional errors and bot-score impact were reported during broader recovery.

open_questions.question: What specific technical fault initiated the degradation?
open_questions.why_open: The updates identify an internal service degradation and later say a fix was implemented, but do not describe the fault (cloudflare-2025-11-18/u1, cloudflare-2025-11-18/u7).

open_questions.question: Did deliberate hostile activity contribute to the outage?
open_questions.why_open: The updates do not attribute the incident to hostile activity or rule it out; they provide no cause sufficient to decide whether this was an attack (cloudflare-2025-11-18/u1, cloudflare-2025-11-18/u20).

open_questions.question: Which systems or services were affected, and to what extent?
open_questions.why_open: The updates mention intermittent impact, application services, dashboard services, Access, WARP, and bot scores, but do not provide a complete service-by-service impact account (cloudflare-2025-11-18/u1, cloudflare-2025-11-18/u8, cloudflare-2025-11-18/u12, cloudflare-2025-11-18/u17).

open_questions.question: What was the final outcome of the deeper investigation?
open_questions.why_open: The 17:44 update says the investigation was continuing, and the later resolved update has no text supplied (cloudflare-2025-11-18/u21, cloudflare-2025-11-18/u22).
